findings.reason: decimal.js:4535 does accept any object whose toStringTag is '[object Decimal]' (tag at decimal.js:108). That duck typing is there on purpose so instances from Decimal.clone() pass. A plain object only gets in if someone deliberately fakes the internal tag, so this is how the API is designed, not a fault the change adds.
findings.claim: The type guard narrows duck-typed objects with toStringTag '[object Decimal]' to Decimal even though they aren't real instances.
findings.evidence: decimal.d.ts:254 and decimal.global.d.ts:275 now declare `static isDecimal(object: any): object is Decimal;`. Decimal.isDecimal is set to isDecimalInstance (decimal.js:4404), which returns `obj instanceof Decimal || obj && obj.toStringTag === tag || false` (decimal.js:4535) with `tag = '[object Decimal]'` (decimal.js:108). So `{toStringTag: '[object Decimal]'}` returns true, and with this change TypeScript treats that object as a Decimal. The guard is still correct for real instances, including instances from Decimal.clone(), which is the case it is meant for.

findings.reason: package.json:32 runs only `node ./test/test.js`, and the only .ts files are the two .d.ts files, so nothing type-checks the declarations. The runtime isDecimal tests pass the same before and after this change. It's a small test gap, so it stays low.

The only isDecimal tests, in test/modules/isFiniteEtc.js:261-277, check runtime true/false values, which this change doesn't affect, so they pass the same before and after.
